name: jj-concurrent
description: Concurrent multi-agent orchestration on Jujutsu (jj) workspaces: the jj-delegate mechanism, the jj-workspace-worker agent, the jj-absorb amend-after-review step (preview with jj absorb --dry-run, distribute working-copy hunks into their downstack commits, and report where each landed), the jj-pr push-and-PR step (push a bookmark then create-or-update its GitHub PR via gh), the jj-stacked-pr step (open/update a stack of based GitHub PRs from a stitched linear jj stack), the jj-land stack-aware land step (land a stack of GitHub PRs bottom-up — wait for required CI at each step, merge, retarget the next PR's base to trunk, then sync local trunk and tidy merged bookmarks and stale workspaces; orchestrator-only, non-interactive, force-free), the jj-checkpoint/jj-rewind op-log safety net (record a named save point before a risky step, then roll the whole repo back to it via jj op restore), the jj-preview read-only-to-history dev-env step (stand up a throwaway jj workspace at an arbitrary revision via jj workspace add -r, provision its per-workspace environment and a distinct port, run the project dev/app command, report the URL + PID, and tear it down cleanly — never moving bookmarks, pushing, or archiving; orchestrator-only), multi-orchestrator namespacing (per-session agent-plan manifests, per-orchestrator workspace/bookmark prefixes, /jj-fleet unions all sessions, and a stale-state startup sweep — so more than one orchestrator can run in one repo), plus snapshot and guard hooks.
